dishes.n: Sydney Harbour barramundi with salsa verde
dishes.make_ahead: Make the salsa verde up to 1 day ahead and keep it covered in the fridge; cook the potatoes and fish on the night

ingredients.item: lemon, juiced, for the salsa verde
barramundi fillets, skin on, about 180g each

steps.text: Boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.
Finely chop the parsley, mint, capers and garlic and stir with the mustard, lemon juice, extra virgin olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Drain the potatoes and crush lightly with the olive oil, lemon zest and salt. Keep warm.
Score the fish skin, pat dry and season with salt.
Cook the fish skin side down in the hot oil, pressing flat, until crisp, then flip to finish.
Serve the fish on the potatoes with the salsa verde spooned over.

s.note: Garlic and chilli prawns sizzled in olive oil with smoked paprika, parsley, lemon and crusty bread
s.how: Peel 600g green prawns, leaving the tails on, pat dry and season with 0.5 tsp salt. Warm 125ml olive oil with 6 sliced garlic cloves and 1 tsp chilli flakes in a wide pan over low heat for 5 to 6 minutes until the garlic is pale gold. Turn the heat up, add the prawns and 1 tsp smoked paprika and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, turning once, until just pink. Stir through half a cup of chopped parsley, squeeze over a lemon and serve sizzling in the pan with torn baguette for the oil.

s.note: Pork and fennel sausage rolls in flaky puff pastry with sesame seeds and tomato sauce
s.how: Heat the oven to 200C and line two trays. Mix 500g pork mince with 1 finely grated onion, 1 tsp toasted and crushed fennel seeds, half a cup of fresh breadcrumbs, 1 egg, 1 tsp salt and 0.5 tsp black pepper. Cut 3 thawed sheets of puff pastry in half, lay a log of filling along each strip, roll up and seal underneath. Chill for 15 minutes, then brush with a second beaten egg, sprinkle with 1 tbsp sesame seeds and cut each log into 4. Bake for 25 minutes until puffed and deep golden, rest 5 minutes and serve with half a cup of tomato sauce.

m.n: Sydney Harbour barramundi with salsa verde
m.note: Crisp-skinned barramundi on crushed lemon potatoes with parsley, mint and caper salsa verde
m.how: Boil 800g baby potatoes in salted water for 20 minutes until tender. Finely chop 1 cup flat-leaf parsley, half a cup of mint, 2 tbsp capers and 1 garlic clove, and stir with 1 tsp dijon mustard, the juice of 1 lemon, 125ml extra virgin olive oil and a pinch of salt. Drain the potatoes and crush lightly with 2 tbsp olive oil, the zest of another lemon and salt. Score the skin of 4 barramundi fillets, pat dry and season. Cook skin side down in 1 tbsp olive oil in a hot pan, pressing flat, for 5 minutes until crisp, then flip for 2 minutes. Serve on the potatoes with the salsa verde spooned over.

w.note: Crisp marshmallow pavlova piled with whipped cream, mango, kiwifruit and passionfruit
w.how: Heat the oven to 150C and draw a 20cm circle on baking paper on a tray. Whisk 4 egg whites to soft peaks, then add 220g caster sugar a spoonful at a time and whisk until thick, glossy and smooth. Fold in 2 tsp cornflour, 1 tsp white vinegar and 1 tsp vanilla. Spread inside the circle with a slight hollow in the middle. Turn the oven down to 120C and bake for 75 minutes, then turn it off and leave the pavlova to cool in the oven with the door ajar. Whip 300ml thickened cream with 1 tbsp icing sugar, pile on top and finish with 1 sliced mango, 2 sliced kiwifruit and the pulp of 4 passionfruit.

d.note: Fino sherry shaken with orange, lemon and sugar syrup over crushed ice with orange, raspberries and mint
d.how: Stir 60g caster sugar into 60ml hot water until dissolved and cool. Shake 240ml fino sherry with the juice of 1 orange, the juice of 1 lemon, the syrup and a scoop of ice, in two batches. Strain into 4 glasses packed with crushed ice and garnish with half wheels of a second orange, 125g raspberries and mint sprigs.
